### policy_conflict_scan

Structured policy in force: 14 base policies + 6 extended policies (`service_ext_completed_call_labor_charge`, `service_ext_arrears_late_fee`, `service_ext_missed_response_credit`, `service_ext_account_settlement_figure`, `service_ext_credit_ceiling_review`, `service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price`).

Overlapping subjects, judged pairwise across the six extended policies:

- `service_invoice_charged` is the subject of the labor charge policy (charge_type labor) and of the late fee policy (charge_type late_fee); the two write disjoint charge kinds through different tools and compute different quantities; the settlement policy reads both. No conflict.
- `service_payment_received` is written only by the settlement policy's tool (`record_account_payment_d97a44a1`). `service_credit_issued` only by the credit policy's tool. `service_program_updated` only by the ceiling review tool. `service_block_hours_purchased` only by the purchase tool. Each subject has one writer.
- Time anchors: all six policies read `NOW` as the handling day; "the current program year" is defined identically in the credit, settlement and ceiling policies (from `term_start_date` to the handling day, implemented as `within_months=MONTHS(F('term_start_date'), NOW)+1`); the late fee and purchase policies use a fixed twelve-month window; the settlement policy a 24-month ledger window. No two policies define the same named window differently.
- Eligibility/status: none of the six extended rules gates on program status; the base dispatch rule's status gate concerns dispatch, not these writes. No conflict.
- Cross-category reads: all five policies that read another category read `maintenance` only, and each declares it in `cross_category` (labor: branch; late fee: history; credit: branch; ceiling: history; purchase: existence). The settlement policy declares none and reads none. Declared reads and compute reads agree (checked binding by binding: CPARAM/CFIELD/EXISTS/XSUM calls name only 'maintenance').
- Terminal states: each policy's tool leaves one new row or one updated row; no two policies write the same field of the same row.

Claimed scopes of the M=2 tasks (the tree of each task is derived in its own file from the `prerequisite` graph and confirmed against the world there): the graph has two weakly connected components — {settlement ← labor, late_fee, credit; credit ← labor} and {purchase ← ceiling}. Any task rooted at settlement spans the first component (4 policies); any task rooted at purchase spans the second (2 policies). The two components are disjoint and together cover all six extended policies. Mutually exclusive and jointly complete — PASS, conditional on each task file confirming its root.

Findings from this scan that are RED or observations are listed under `findings` (F1–F3 concern base/extended conflicts and are recorded under `override_declarations`).

### rule_compute_equivalence

Method: for each policy every `compute` binding was matched against its `compute_basis` quotation and that quotation located verbatim in the `rule`; then every rule sentence was swept back to a binding.

`service_ext_completed_call_labor_charge` — 18 bindings. Every quantity (logged hours, band, premium, minimum, agreement coverage/rate/site, call site, priority, technician count, further-technician rate, unexpired block hours, hours drawn in span, term block hours, term hours drawn, chargeable hours, rounding) has a verbatim `compute_basis` sentence present in the rule. Ladders: `hours_charged_for` (3 tiers), `governing_labor_rate` (3), `further_technician_rate` (3), `band_premium` (3), `prepaid_hours_offset` (3) — each tier is a rule sentence and a branch of the `decides` binding. Rounding "to the nearest cent, half up" is implemented by `RND` = Python `round`, which is banker's rounding on exact ties (observation O1, charter-wide). Sweep back: no rule sentence without a binding; no binding without a rule sentence. PASS (see F1/F2 for base conflicts, which are not rule/compute mismatches).

`service_ext_arrears_late_fee` — 16 bindings. Window ("twelve months to the day the fee is raised" → `within_months=K('fee_window_months')`), exclusion of undated charges (implemented by `_within` returning False on an empty `due_date`), fee base ladder, months ladder, rate ladder (suspension period / payment term / credit limit), other-account step (XSUM over maintenance installments and payments), handling charge ladder, result grouping and rounding — all quoted verbatim. One point checked closely: the rule's "the payments received in it leave part of the invoiced total standing" is implemented as `fee_base > 0`, which is also true when no payment was received at all; the sentence's plain reading covers that case (nothing paid leaves the whole standing). PASS.

`service_ext_missed_response_credit` — 15 bindings. Labor element ladder (line stands / no line and no blocks / hours × block rate), attendance ladder (waived / lower published trip charge / tier trip charge), severity ladder (priority × later calendar day), repeat uplift ladder (≥3 / exactly 2 / otherwise), program-year window, cap applied after rounding — all quoted verbatim; `days_to_arrival >= 1` implements "a later calendar day" through `DAYS` on the date parts. PASS.

`service_ext_account_settlement_figure` — 15 bindings. Charges ladder (undated + fallen due → all; none fallen due but undated → undated only; otherwise fallen due within the 24-month ledger window), credits ladder, emergency element ladder, allowance ladder, allowance on charges taken in alone — all quoted verbatim. The second charges tier is implemented as `charges_all - charges_due` under `charges_due <= 0`, which equals "only the charges awaiting a due day". PASS.

`service_ext_credit_ceiling_review` — 19 bindings. Review-window ladder (reinstated / less than a term / twelve months), starting-ceiling ladder, portfolio ladder (XSUM over maintenance), volume ladder, single-factor combination with the allowance added afterwards — quoted verbatim and implemented as stated. **Correction recorded during the freeze of task 1 (before any reveal): the payment-record and arrears ladders are NOT equivalent in both directions.** The rule's tiers read "no invoice on the program has stood past its due day longer than the tier's suspension period" (payment_record tiers 1 and 2), "an invoice has stood past its due day longer than the tier's suspension period" (arrears tier 1) and "an invoice stands past its due day" (arrears tier 2) — each quantifies over every invoice on the program. The compute binds `days_past_due = DAYS(LATEST('service_events','due_date', …), NOW)`, the age of the single most recently due invoice, and tests only that. An older invoice that stands unpaid past the suspension period while the latest invoice is fresh satisfies the prose and not the compute. **F6 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (rule/compute).** Consequence demonstrated in task 1's file. The late fee and settlement policies write "the most recent invoice to fall due" explicitly and are consistent.

`service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price` — 23 bindings. Drawing-window ladder, block-size ladder, stepped-rate ladder (EXISTS maintenance), price-basis ladder, release-rate ladder, settlement-discount ladder, discount on block price alone — quoted verbatim. Observation O2: the baseline sentence "A block of prepaid hours is sold in one of the tier's minimum purchase multiples" is the prose for `multiples = K('one_multiple')`; the sentence is readable as "one multiple" only with the `one_multiple` parameter beside it. **Correction recorded during the freeze of task 1 (before any reveal): the rule never defines "the open position".** The rule says "The headroom is the credit ceiling standing on the rate program less the open position" and "no open position stands on the program" / "an open position does stand", but no sentence of this policy states what the open position is; the compute binds `open_position = invoiced_all - paid_all` (every invoice and every payment on the program, no window), and `compute_basis` for `invoiced_all`, `paid_all` and `open_position` quotes only the headroom sentence, which does not say it. The late fee policy defines its open position over a twelve-month window; the program row carries a `balance_due` field; a reader has at least three candidates. Compute invents a basis the rule does not state. **F5 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (rule/compute).** Consequence demonstrated in task 1's file. The release-rate tiers ("an invoice stands past its due day") carry the same existential-prose / latest-only-compute gap as F6, recorded under F6.

### prerequisite_sentences

Four-point test per edge (connective; record-visible state in the tables' words with no actor/tool; no tool/policy id/snake_case/row id; strength equal to `condition`):

E1 credit ← labor: "The credit for a missed response is worked out only once the labor charge for the call it arises from stands invoiced on the demand service account." — connective "only once"; state = a labor charge invoiced on the account (service_events, event_type service_invoice_charged, charge_type labor); no identifiers; strength equals `condition` ("A demand service charge line of the labor kind stands on the rate program for the call the credit arises from"). Exactly one write of this difficulty creates a labor-kind charge line: `charge_demand_labor_invoice_877d69f1` (the late fee tool writes charge_type late_fee; the purchase tool writes a block purchase row). Derivation for the reader: the sentence names the state; the labor policy's own rule opens "The labor line for demand work is raised for the call last completed on the rate program" — the only rule in the charter that raises a labor line — so the resolving action is that policy's write. Single reading. The labor rule does not restate the sentence. PASS.

E2 settlement ← labor: "The figure that clears the demand service account is settled only once every call completed on the program carries its labor charge on the ledger." — connective "only once"; state form; no identifiers; strength equals the declared `condition` ("Every call completed on the rate program carries a demand service charge line of the labor kind on the ledger"). Resolving write unique as in E1. Observation O3: the sentence and the condition quantify over every completed call, while the depended-on policy prices only "the call last completed on the rate program" and its tool books one line per call; after the one resolving write the state as worded is still false wherever earlier completed calls carry no labor line. The reader is led to the resolving write in one reading because the charter offers no method to price any other call; but the gate as written is not brought about by `resolved_by`. Recorded as an observation (no computable second figure), each task file states whether its world has earlier completed calls without labor lines.

E3 settlement ← late fee: "The figure that clears the demand service account is settled only after the late fee the billing month owes stands as a line on the rate program." — "only after"; state = a late-fee-kind charge line for the billing month; unique writer `charge_overdue_late_fee_58988cf8`; strength equals `condition`. PASS.

E4 settlement ← credit: "The figure that clears the demand service account is settled only after the credit owed for a response recorded as missed stands as a credit entry on the rate program." — "only after"; state = a service_credit_issued row with credit_reason missed_response; unique writer `credit_missed_response_9859bc76`; strength equals `condition`. PASS. Observation O4 (charter-level, consequence judged per task): "the credit owed for a response recorded as missed" is singular, while a world may carry several completed calls with `sla_met = missed` and no credit; the credit policy's bindings are all `LATEST`, so only the most recent call's credit is computable — earlier misses cannot be priced from this charter.

E5 purchase ← ceiling: "A block of prepaid hours is priced only once the credit ceiling standing on the rate program carries a change dated in the current program year." — "only once"; state = service_programs.last_change_type = credit_limit_changed with last_change_date inside the current program year (the words of the `service_program_updated` event: last_change_type, last_change_date); no identifiers; strength equals `condition`. Exactly one write of this difficulty stamps a term change on the program: `set_program_credit_ceiling_aca954d3` (`ctx.update(... last_change_type="credit_limit_changed", last_change_date=now)`). The ceiling policy's own rule opens "The open balance ceiling written on a rate program at review is worked out … and it replaces the ceiling the program carried" — the only rule that writes the ceiling. Single reading. PASS.

No rule states a cross-problem order that grounds no declared edge (each of the six rules was read for ordering connectives joined to another problem's result: only the five sentences above). No rule names another policy's tool. No depended-on rule restates a prerequisite sentence. No base sentence grounds an edge.

### override_declarations

Sentence-by-sentence against each `base_policy_refs` entry; the criterion is the quantity that gets scored.

**service_ext_completed_call_labor_charge** (refs: service_labor_billing, service_billing_and_late_fee, service_portfolio_interaction; overwrite names one sentence of service_labor_billing — the band multiplier sentence).

- service_labor_billing S1 "Labor on a demand call is billed at the tier's regular rate for the lead technician, at the second journeyman rate for each further journeyman and at the apprentice rate for an apprentice, each for the hours that person was on site." — Lead rate: extended uses "the tier's block overage rate"; the two parameters are numerically equal in all six tiers (165/152/144/138/132/126), so no scored difference. Further technicians: base prices by the person's grade and "for the hours that person was on site"; extended prices by the call's priority (second journeyman rate on emergency/critical, apprentice rate on routine/priority) and "for the hours charged for" (the minimum where the logged hours fall short). **Handled differently, not named in `overwrite` — undeclared override (F1).** Consequence exists on any world with more than one technician where the logged hours fall short of the minimum or the call is routine/priority with a journeyman: demonstrated per task.
- S2 band multipliers — named in `overwrite`; replacement unique (weekend hours now carry the after-hours multiplier; numerically equal in every tier). Declared. PASS.
- S3 regular hours definition — extended reads the band from the record. Follows.
- S4 minimum billable / after-hours minimum / quarter-hour rounding up — extended follows (billable_hours). PASS.
- S5 trip charge once per call, diagnostic once per work order, credited diagnostic — extended's labor line carries neither; base service_billing_and_late_fee B1 puts trip and diagnostic on separate lines, so the labor line legitimately excludes them. Follows. Observation O5: the base `formula` `labor_charge_usd = round(max(minimum_billable_hours, labor_hours) * regular_labor_rate_usd * after_hours_rate_multiplier + trip_charge_usd, 2)` adds the trip charge into `labor_charge_usd`, contradicting B1's separate lines; extended's `labor_charge_usd` excludes it and does not name the formula. Base rule B1 supports extended, so this is recorded as an observation on the base formula, not as an override.
- S6 travel time — the Block Hour tier does not bill it; extended takes the logged hours as they stand. Follows.
- S7 parts and refrigerant — separate lines. n/a.
- service_billing_and_late_fee B1 separate lines — followed. B2 "The invoice falls due the tier's payment term after the invoice date" — the labor tool writes `due_date=""`; see F3 under the settlement policy. B3/B4 — n/a to the labor line.
- service_portfolio_interaction P1 (covered unit → program bills nothing) — extended tier 1 follows, with the site match. P2 "Where the tier allows rate substitution and the unit sits on a maintenance agreement that does not cover the repair, the lower of the agreement's labor rate and this program's labor rate governs" — extended tier 2 follows the "lower of" rule but (a) does not test the site match base states for tier 2 and (b) does not test the tier's `maintenance_holder_rate_substitution` flag (P3). (b) never changes a number: tier 2 only fires for agreements that do not cover repair labor (Filter & Belt 148, Inspection 142, Preventive 136), all above the overage rates of the two no-substitution tiers (132, 126). Observation O6: on a world where the account's active non-covering agreement runs at a different building from the call, base P2 ("the unit sits on a maintenance agreement") keeps the program rate while extended tier 2 substitutes the agreement rate; no `overwrite` names P2/P3. Consequence judged per task.
- **service_block_hour_drawdown is not in `base_policy_refs` and not in `overwrite`, yet the extended rule prices the prepaid-hours offset.** Base D1 "they are drawn down by the labor hours of each completed call, oldest block first" and D4 "Unused hours expire at the tier's expiry period counted forward in whole calendar months from the day the block was bought" define per-block, oldest-first drawdown with per-block expiry, and D3 "Once the remaining block reaches zero the further hours of that call and of every later call are billed at the tier's overage rate". Extended: "the prepaid hours available to the call are the hours of every block bought within that period less the hours drawn by the calls completed in the same period ahead of it" — an aggregate over a trailing window that ignores hours absorbed by blocks now outside the window. The two methods give different chargeable hours whenever a block older than the expiry window absorbed draws that fall inside it. **Undeclared override (F2).** Consequence demonstrated per task.

**service_ext_arrears_late_fee** (refs: service_billing_and_late_fee, service_labor_billing, service_portfolio_interaction; overwrite names B3).

- B3 per-invoice, per-month late fee — named; replacement (one fee line for the billing month on the twelve-month window) is unique. Declared. PASS.
- B2 due date — the fee tool writes `due_date=""`; the extended rule itself says "Charges the office has raised but not yet dated for payment do not enter it" — internally consistent, and the fee's own base excludes undated lines so no second late-fee figure arises. See F3 for the settlement consequence.
- B4 payments to the oldest invoice unless directed — n/a to the fee amount. service_labor_billing and service_portfolio_interaction — no sentence governs the fee. Follows.

**service_ext_missed_response_credit** (ref: service_response_guarantee_credit; overwrite names R3).

- R1 credited where the technician is later than the guarantee — extended prices "the call it arises from" and reads the missed count from `sla_met = missed`; follows. R2 elapsed-hours counting — n/a to the amount. R3 credit = rate × labor charge, capped — named; replacement unique. R4 no credit on denied access / unreachable caller / credit-limit hold — inherited, extended silent (each task file checks the world for such evidence). R5 zero-rate tier — inherited. Base formula — replaced by the declared sentence. PASS.

**service_ext_account_settlement_figure** (ref: service_billing_and_late_fee; overwrite `[]`).

- B1 separate lines — followed (charges summed line by line).
- **B2 "The invoice falls due the tier's payment term after the invoice date, counted in calendar days with the invoice day excluded and the due day included, and the account's own credit terms apply only where the program has no term of its own."** Extended: "Where charges stand on the program that have not yet been given a due day and charges also stand that have fallen due, every charge invoiced on the program is taken in, dated for payment or not; where no charge on the program has fallen due but charges stand awaiting a due day, only the charges awaiting a due day are taken in." Under B2 every invoice carries a due day fixed by rule at issue; a charge "not yet given a due day" does not exist, and a line issued on the handling day has not fallen due, so under the baseline sentence "Only the charges that have fallen due are taken in" it is excluded. The labor and late fee tools write `due_date=""`, and the extended ladder reads that blank as the tier selector. The quantity scored (the figure that clears the account) differs between the two readings whenever a line was raised on the handling day. **Undeclared override (F3).** Consequence demonstrated per task.
- B3 late fee — the settlement takes the fee line in as a charge; follows. B4 — n/a.
- service_emergency_entitlement is not referenced: extended's "emergency dispatch element" charges the surcharge per dispatch beyond the included calls (base: "it carries the tier's emergency surcharge") and at heavy use 1.5× the surcharge (base: no multiple). Observation O7: the heavy-use tier deviates from the base surcharge without a reference; it changes a number only when dispatches exceed twice the included calls — judged per task.

**service_ext_credit_ceiling_review** (ref: service_quote_and_approval; overwrite `[]`). No sentence of service_quote_and_approval governs the credit ceiling; the base rule on the ceiling is service_suspension_and_reinstatement ("as soon as the open balance passes the tier's credit limit") and service_dispatch_and_response ("A call at an account over the tier's credit limit is held"), neither of which fixes the ceiling's amount. Extended replaces the amount by review. No conflict on a scored quantity. PASS (observation O8: the declared base ref is unrelated to the subject).

**service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price** (ref: service_block_hour_drawdown; overwrite names D1).

- D1 "bought in multiples of the tier's minimum purchase at the tier's block rate, and they are drawn down … oldest block first" — named in full; replacement fixes the size sold. The rate part ("at the tier's block rate") is superseded by the same declaration, so the stepped bulk/volume rate is declared. The drawdown part of D1 is superseded with nothing put in its place for drawdown; the purchase policy's `hours_drawn`/`balance_now` use the aggregate window method. Declared at sentence level. PASS.
- D2 face value whatever band — followed. D4 expiry in whole calendar months — `blocks_bought` within `block_hour_expiry_months` follows. D5 rollover — used in the window ladder. D3/D6 — n/a. PASS.

| ceiling review | 6 | 4 (payment_record, arrears_position, portfolio_position, call_volume_allowance) | 2 (review_window, starting_ceiling) | review_window (term run ∧ reinstatement), payment_record (payment count ∧ days past due), arrears_position (days past due ∧ invoiced−paid vs limit; ∧ invoice count), portfolio_position (agreement price ∧ installments vs payments), call_volume_allowance (dispatch count ∧ emergency count) | portfolio_position → maintenance (CFIELD annual_price_usd, XSUM installments/payments) |
| block purchase | 6 | 3 (stepped_block_rate, office_release_rate, settlement_record_discount) | 3 (block_size_sold, drawing_record_window, price_basis) | drawing_record_window (rollover ∧ term run), stepped_block_rate (multiples ∧ agreement), price_basis (multiples ∧ blocks standing), office_release_rate (excess ∧ days past due), settlement_record_discount (payments vs invoiced ∧ open position) | stepped_block_rate → maintenance (EXISTS status active) |

Per policy: 4–6 factors, ≥2 parameter, ≥1 method — all six satisfy the bounds. Per task the multi-source and cross-difficulty floors are met by the tree's policies (each component contains at least one of each); confirmed per task in `factor_weight`.

Structure checks, all six policies: every factor's `decides` is an input binding, never `result`; binding sets are pairwise disjoint within each policy; every ladder has exactly three pairwise-disjoint tiers (the first two conditioned, the third "otherwise"); every tier's condition and outcome is stated as a sentence of the `rule` and implemented as a branch of the `decides` binding; every method tier names a computation the rule states. No two tiers of one ladder select the same value or method — checked value by value (arrears rate 2.0 / 1.75 / tier late fee; uplift 1.25 / 1.1 / 1.0; release 3.0 / 1.5 / 0; discount 2.0 / 1.0 / 0; and so on) — **with one exception, corrected during the freeze of task 1 (before any reveal): `price_basis` (purchase policy).** Tier 2 "where two or three multiples are sold, the whole block is priced at the rate the block steps to" and the fall-through "the whole block is priced at the tier's block hour rate" select the same value on every world where tier 2 fires, because the `stepped_block_rate` ladder steps the rate only "where the multiples sold stand at or above the bulk multiple count" (4); for two or three multiples the rate the block steps to is the tier's block hour rate itself. Tier 2 is therefore one tier written as two. **F4 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED (unreal ladder), charter-level; whether the tier taken on a task is that tier is stated in the task file.** Observation O14: `emergency_dispatch_element` (settlement) has a fall-through of 0 per dispatch on a domain where the multiplier (dispatches beyond the included calls) is itself 0, so the fall-through's value cannot be observed; its value nonetheless differs from tier 2's and the baseline substitution changes the result wherever tier 2 fires — accepted as real. Labels honest: each `method` factor changes the algorithm (which window, which rows, which pricing basis) and each `parameter` factor substitutes a number into the same formula. Every fall-through tier is the factor's `baseline` and the baseline value is what `baseline.rule` states for that input — with one exception, observation O9:

- O9 (`further_technician_rate`, labor policy): `baseline.rule` carries "Where the call was worked by more than one technician, nothing further is billed for the technicians beyond the lead." while the ladder's two live tiers both require more than one technician and its fall-through ("otherwise") is the one-technician case. The baseline sentence therefore asserts, of exactly the situations the two live tiers cover, the opposite outcome. Numerically the baseline value (0.0) is the fall-through value, so `baseline.params` and the substitution are coherent; but the rule carries two adjacent sentences that reach different figures on every multi-technician world. Every other baseline sentence of the charter is either unconditional or identical to its fall-through. Whether this hands a task a second answer is demonstrated in that task's file.

Business realism of conditions and outcomes (each tier condition weighed for whether an HVAC service contractor settling that quantity would weigh it, and whether it holds of every customer reaching the write): after-hours minimum vs logged hours; agreement coverage and published agreement rate; call priority for the grade of the second technician; band premium; prepaid block offset by rollover tier; arrears rate stepped by suspension period and credit limit; months from last payment or last due date; fee base net of payments; a step for the owner's other account standing; a handling charge for multiple overdue invoices; credit severity by priority and next-day arrival; repeat-miss uplift; charges and credits taken in by dating; surcharge beyond included emergencies; settlement allowance for prompt payers; ceiling review by invoiced volume, payment record, arrears, portfolio and call volume; block size from the drawing record; bulk/volume stepped rates; release charge on excess over headroom; good-payer discount — none holds of every customer who reaches the write, and each is a distinction a contractor's credit and billing desk actually draws. One reservation, observation O10: the `settlement_allowance_rate` fall-through ("no allowance comes off") is the ordinary treatment, and the 1.5% allowance for accounts whose latest invoice is within the suspension period with payments on file is a prompt-settlement discount some contractors publish; accepted as real. Observation O11: the labor policy's `hours_charged_for` fall-through ("hours as logged, rounded up to the quarter hour") is the base's own method, so its baseline is honest.

### findings

- **F1 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (undeclared override, service_labor_billing S1, further technicians).** Symptom: two prices for the technician beyond the lead. Root cause: extended prices further technicians by call priority and "for the hours charged for"; base S1 prices "each further journeyman" and "an apprentice" by grade "for the hours that person was on site"; `overwrite` names only the band sentence. Evidence: service.yaml policy service_labor_billing rule S1 (quoted above); service.extended.yaml service_ext_completed_call_labor_charge rule "Where the call record shows more than one technician on a call taken at emergency or critical priority, each technician beyond the lead is billed at the tier's second journeyman rate for the hours charged for" and `overwrite[0].superseded_clause` (band sentence only). Consequence: demonstrated in each task whose world carries a call with `technician_count > 1` (task files). Affected artifact: service.extended.yaml, service_ext_completed_call_labor_charge.overwrite / rule.
- **F2 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (undeclared override, service_block_hour_drawdown D1/D3/D4, prepaid drawdown).** Symptom: two chargeable-hour figures for the same call. Root cause: extended computes the prepaid offset as an aggregate over a trailing window; base draws oldest block first with per-block expiry; service_block_hour_drawdown is neither in `base_policy_refs` nor in `overwrite` of the labor policy. Evidence: quoted under override_declarations. Consequence: demonstrated per task where a block older than the expiry window absorbed draws inside it. Affected: service.extended.yaml, service_ext_completed_call_labor_charge (base_policy_refs, overwrite, rule sentences on prepaid hours).
- **F3 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (undeclared override, service_billing_and_late_fee B2, undated charges).** Symptom: two settlement figures depending on whether a line raised on the handling day is "awaiting a due day" or "falls due thirty days after the invoice date and has not fallen due". Root cause: the settlement ladder's first two tiers and the tools' `due_date=""` presuppose undated invoices; base B2 dates every invoice at issue; `overwrite` is `[]`. Evidence: quoted under override_declarations; task_tools.py `charge_demand_labor_invoice_877d69f1` and `charge_overdue_late_fee_58988cf8` both `create(... due_date="")`. Consequence: demonstrated per task rooted at settlement. Affected: service.extended.yaml, service_ext_account_settlement_figure.overwrite / rule; task_tools.py (the two `due_date=""` effects).
- **F4 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED (unreal ladder, `price_basis`, purchase policy).** See factor_ladders: tier 2 and the fall-through select the same value on tier 2's whole domain. Affected: service.extended.yaml, service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price.factors[price_basis] and the rule sentence "where two or three multiples are sold, the whole block is priced at the rate the block steps to".
- **F5 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (rule/compute, "the open position" undefined in the purchase policy).** See rule_compute_equivalence. Affected: service.extended.yaml, service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price.rule / compute (`invoiced_all`, `paid_all`, `open_position`) / compute_basis.
- **F6 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (rule/compute, existential prose vs latest-only compute in the ceiling review's payment-record and arrears ladders; same gap in the purchase policy's release-rate ladder).** See rule_compute_equivalence. Affected: service.extended.yaml, service_ext_credit_ceiling_review.rule / compute (`days_past_due`, `payment_record_step`, `arrears_cut`); service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price (`days_past_due`, `release_rate`).
- O1 — observation: `RND` is Python `round` (banker's rounding on exact binary ties) while every rule says "half up"; consequence only on an exact tie — each task file states whether any scored figure sits on one.
- O2 — observation: purchase baseline sentence "sold in one of the tier's minimum purchase multiples" reads as "one multiple" only with `one_multiple` beside it.
- O3 — observation: E2's sentence/condition quantify over every completed call; the resolving write books one line; the gate as worded is not made true by `resolved_by` where earlier calls carry no labor line.
- O4 — observation: earlier calls with `sla_met = missed` and no credit cannot be priced by the credit policy (all bindings `LATEST`); base R1 says such customers are credited.
- O5 — observation: base service_labor_billing `formula` folds the trip charge into `labor_charge_usd`, against B1; extended excludes it, consistent with B1.
- O6 — observation: extended tier 2 of `governing_labor_rate` omits the site match and the substitution flag base P2/P3 state; a number changes only on worlds where the agreement runs at another building or a no-substitution tier holds a Full Coverage / Comprehensive agreement.
- O7 — observation: settlement's heavy-use 1.5× surcharge multiple has no base reference; bites only above twice the included calls.
- O8 — observation: service_ext_credit_ceiling_review's base ref (service_quote_and_approval) does not govern its subject.
- O9 — observation (see factor_ladders): `further_technician_rate` baseline sentence states the complement of its fall-through.
- O10/O11 — realism notes above.

Each task file cites this section by path and heading and demonstrates F1–F6 against its own world where they bite.
